messages:
max: FYI customers are seeing p99 spikes after we onboarded orchidflux-v1. Mostly triggered on long-context jobs (~8k+ tokens) and when the prompt includes heavy code blocks. Noticed 3x p99 vs baseline. Posting a quick repro and logs.

anya: ugh, saw alerts at 14:10 PST. p95 unchanged, p99 shot up. Could be tokenizer boundary changes from the new BPE merges? :eyes:

sam: can you paste the curl you used to repro? also did we change batching or KV cache behavior for the new model?

max: repro curl below — simple single request to hosted API with long prompt. fails consistently for >8k.

max: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"orchidflux-v1","input":"<long_prompt_here>... (8k tokens) ...","max_tokens":512,"stream":false}'```

max: From traces: tail of request spends ~600ms in tokenizer splitting and an extra ~900ms in runtime while building KV slices. Also seeing a lot of kvcache misses flagged as "boundary_rewrite" in logs.

luis: tagging eng-oncall. @sam can you check whether the tokenizer mapping table for orchidflux-v1 differs? might be added merges causing more split ops on code fences.

sam: looking. The onboarding config included new merge rules to support extra unicode sequences. I pushed a heuristic that tries to avoid long contiguous tokens, could be causing more resharding. digging into commit 3f7a9.

anya: metrics: compare window 30m before vs after deploy. p99 was 2200ms -> 6800ms on affected endpoints. Throughput unchanged. So not infra saturation.

ops-bot: Incident alert: support/p99-spike orchidflux-v1 - triggered 3071110400. Channel: #support.

luis: likely culprit = tokenizer boundary changes + KV split causing extra kernel launches for long context. If tokenizer now produces different chunk boundaries, runtime may be forced into more KV recompute.

sam: quick mitigation options: 1) route long-context requests to orchidflux-v1-compat (older tokenizer) 2) revert the merge heuristic 3) increase prefix-KV cache TTL so we can reuse slices 4) force single-token-chunking threshold (less parallelization but fewer reshard ops). Which do we want first?

max: routing to compat sounds lowest risk. Can we do a traffic rule?

sam: yes, I can add a smart-route rule for requests with estimated_input_tokens > 6k to use orchidflux-v1-compat. Will push in next 10m.

anya: while sam does that, can eng-runtime add a quick metric that counts "boundary_rewrite" events per request and correlate with p99? want to prove cause before reverting merges.

sam: will add a temp metric and a trace tag; pushing route now.

(max edits) max: route added, testing shows p99 for routed requests down to ~2.4s. Still investigating a small tail for non-routed though.

luis: should we scale dedicated pools for orchidflux-v1 to see if kernel queueing contributed? Orignal infra looked fine but kernel launches per request increased.

anya: scaling might mask root cause. Prefer routing + metric to confirm. If confirmed, rollback tokenizer heuristic.

sam: metric shows strong correlation: requests with >5 boundary_rewrite events account for 85% of p99 occurrences.

max: awesome — that points at tokenizer. @anya can you take the rollback? I can keep route in place until rollback is live and then run canary.

anya: on it. Rolling back merge heuristic in tokenizer config and kicking off a canary redeploy to 3 hosts. will monitor traces and p99.

ops-bot: Deploy started by anya at 3071112100.

sam: canary looks good after rollback on those hosts: p99 dropped to ~2.1s on canary. No errors.

luis: plan: 1) keep route in place for 60m 2) fully roll tokenizer rollback if canary stable 3) follow up with safer tokenizer integration (add compatibility tests for long-context code fences) 4) add a monitoring regression alert for boundary_rewrite events tied to p99.

max: agreed. I'll notify affected customers and update the ticket with mitigation steps + ETA for full rollback. :thumbsup:

anya: full rollback scheduled in 20m if canary stable.

max: postmortem notes to capture: onboarding checklist missing long-context regression test, missing metric for boundary_rewrite, and need a traffic ramp gate for tokenizer changes.

sam: also add an integration test in runtime that simulates >8k token prompt with code blocks and asserts tokenization boundaries don't cause extra KV splits.

luis: closing loop with infra: no capacity issues, just more kernel invocations. Will run a batch job to profile kernel launch overhead on the path.

max: thanks all. keeping the route until rollback fully rolled out. will post final status.

ops-bot: Incident resolved: p99 regressions reduced after rollback + routing. Final update at 3071112260.
